policy_name: Purchase Order and Payment Approval Limits
content:
Approval limits by role and amount:
- Store Manager: GBP 5,000
- Warehouse Manager: GBP 10,000
- Buyer: GBP 50,000
- Category Manager: GBP 100,000
- Director: GBP 500,000
- CFO/CEO: unlimited
All orders over GBP 1,000 require 2 approvals. All supplier bank detail changes require Finance review.

Put customer on credit hold when:
- Invoice >60 days overdue
- Account balance >GBP 500k
- DSO >90 days
Action: stop shipments, escalate to Credit Controller, contact customer. Release after payment received or payment plan agreed.

For quality non-conformances:
1. High-risk defects (safety, functionality): Immediate hold on all POs. Require corrective action plan within 5 days.
2. Medium-risk defects (cosmetic, minor): Limit POs to 50% of normal volume. Require action plan within 10 days.
3. Low-risk defects (documentation): Monitor and notify supplier within 15 days.
Suspend supplier if repeated issues (>3 in 12 months). Exit if corrective action not implemented within 30 days.

Currency hedging limits:
- USD exposure: hedge 50-80% of 12-month forecast. Max 100%.
- EUR exposure: hedge 40-70% of 12-month forecast. Max 90%.
- Other major currencies: hedge 40-60%. Max 80%.
Instruments allowed: forward contracts, options (call spreads max). Forbid: speculative positions, exotic options.
Review hedge ratios quarterly. Spot rates used for P&L; mark hedges at forward rates.

All suppliers must maintain:
- General Liability: min GBP 2m (high-risk) or GBP 500k (low-risk)
- Product Liability: min GBP 5m (food/apparel) or GBP 1m (other)
- Cyber Liability: min GBP 1m (if data access)
- Cargo Insurance: min 110% of shipment value
- All policies: evidence of coverage required at onboarding and annually

Requirements by risk tier:
HIGH-RISK (emerging markets, new sector, high spend):
- Social and ethical audit (BSCI or equivalent) required before first order
- Business registration and tax ID verification
- Bank references (3 suppliers)
- Insurance evidence (GL 2m+, PL 5m+)
- Sanctions screening required
MEDIUM-RISK (developed market, established sector):
- Audit within 12 months of first order
- Business registration verification
- Bank references (2 suppliers)
- Insurance evidence (GL 1m+, PL 2m+)
LOW-RISK (existing supplier, low spend):
- Basic compliance check
- Insurance verification
- Annual audit if spend >GBP 500k

Inventory ownership: Transfer of title at receipt into our DC (not in-transit). In-transit goods remain supplier's responsibility until gate-in.
Status definitions:
- Available: ready for picking or sale
- In-transit: on PO, not yet received
- Reserved: allocated to open orders
- Damaged: non-saleable, awaiting write-off approval
Valuation: FIFO method. Seasonal stock over 180 days old to be marked down 25% minimum per NRV rules.

When allegations of forced labour or serious violations arise:
1. IMMEDIATE (within 24 hours): Escalate to General Counsel and Ethics Officer. Secure evidence.
2. WITHIN 5 DAYS: Assess credibility (review original reporting, NGO corroboration, supply chain connection). Interview factory if credible.
3. WITHIN 10 DAYS: Decide on hold/suspension/exit. Communicate decision to affected functions (Sourcing, Finance, Supply Chain).
Do NOT communicate to media or public without Legal approval.
Document all steps and findings for regulatory response.

Approved fallback positions by clause (standard / first fallback / red line):
- Limitation of liability: Standard: cap at amounts paid in the previous 12 months, with product safety, injury, IP and data breach uncapped. First fallback: cap at 100% of the value of the affected order for general claims. Red line: never cap product safety, death or personal injury, IP infringement or data breach.
- IP ownership: Standard: Buyer owns all designs, patterns and improvements. First fallback: supplier keeps pre-existing IP and Buyer gets a royalty-free perpetual licence to improvements. Red line: supplier must not own or resell Buyer designs.
- Force majeure: Standard: excludes strikes, supplier financial failure and shipping delays; 48-hour notice; either party may terminate after 90 days. First fallback: 120 days before termination. Red line: no relief for supplier financial failure or foreseeable shipping delay.
- Payment terms: Standard: 60 days from goods receipt. First fallback: 45 days. Red line: never faster than 30 days and no payment before shipment.
- Termination: Standard: termination for convenience on 90 days' notice. First fallback: 180 days notice on volume-committed frameworks. Red line: no termination fee beyond finished goods and materials bought against firm orders.
- Audit and code of conduct: Standard: unannounced audit right and signed supplier code of conduct. First fallback: 5 working days' notice. Red line: no audit right means no agreement.
- Subcontracting: Standard: only with written consent. First fallback: pre-approved subcontractor list. Red line: no unauthorised subcontracting.
- Volume commitment: Standard: 60% of forecast with +/-20% flexibility. First fallback: 70% with +/-15%. Red line: no commitment above 70% of forecast and no agreement without a flexibility band.

QUALITY INCIDENT:
- Severity 1 (safety): Immediate hold, exec escalation, customer notification within 4 hours
- Severity 2 (functionality): 24-hour response, manager escalation, customer notification within 24 hours
- Severity 3 (cosmetic): 5-day response, team escalation
SUPPLY CHAIN INCIDENT (geopolitical, transport, supplier failure):
- Tier 1 (affects delivery <72 hours): Escalate to VP Supply Chain immediately
- Tier 2 (affects delivery 3-7 days): Manager escalation, sourcing team response
- Tier 3 (future impact): Monitor and document
SECURITY INCIDENT:
- CISO involvement mandatory. Supplier user account compromise: lock account, block payments, audit access logs.

policy_name: Legal Guidance on Admissions and Claims Wording
content:
Avoid in customer communication, marketing, and internal documents:
- 'Defect' or 'defective' (use 'does not meet spec' or 'variation')
- 'We are responsible for...' (use 'The matter involves...')
- Admitting causation without evidence ('caused by X' without testing)
- Making comparative claims ('better than competitor') without substantiation
- Sustainability claims ('eco-friendly', 'sustainable') without certification
SAFE WORDING:
- 'We are investigating the matter.'
- 'Testing to date indicates...'
- 'Meets ISO 14040 environmental standards.'
- Always include: 'Pending further testing/investigation/legal review.'

policy_name: Lot Acceptance Quality and Release Policy
content:
AQL (Acceptable Quality Level) by defect severity:
- Critical (safety, function): AQL 0.65%, max 1 defect per 100 units sampled
- Major (appearance >2cm, function <spec): AQL 1.5%, max 2 defects per 100 units
- Minor (small appearance): AQL 2.5%, max 3 defects per 100 units
Release decision:
- Results within AQL: Release for sale
- 1 critical defect: Reject entire lot. Request rework or replacement.
- >1 major defect: Conditional release at 20% price reduction if customer accepts
- Sorted and reworked lots: Retest at 2x sample size. All critical defects must be zero.

policy_name: Internal Policy on Market Entry Structures
content:
Market entry structures by region and spend:
UK/EU (mature markets, <GBP 5m annual): Franchise or partnership preferred. Subsidiary if >GBP 50m spend or IP at risk.
Emerging markets (China, India, SE Asia, <GBP 20m): Joint venture with local partner required. IP strictly protected. Exit clause mandatory.
Nearshore (Turkey, Morocco, Mexico, GBP 5-50m): Joint venture or subsidiary. Build IP gradually; don't over-rely on one partner.
Exit: Subsidiary - require 6-month notice, transfer of contracts and staff obligations. JV - buyout clause if partner underperforms.

Assurance requirements for ESG and sustainability reporting:
Scope 1 & 2 Emissions: Annual independent third-party assurance (ISO 14064-3). Acceptable assurance providers: ISAE 3000 accredited bodies.
Scope 3 Emissions: Reasonable assurance required for supply chain emissions >50% of total. Data evidence: supplier questionnaires, shipment records, conversion factors from GHG Protocol.
Supply Chain Disclosures: Annual audit of forced labour due diligence (legal obligation UK MSA 2015). Evidence: supplier audit reports, sanctions screening, grievance records.
Reporting Framework Compliance: All disclosures against TCFD, GRI, SASB standards require management review and sign-off.

policy_name: Supplier Code of Conduct - Wage and Hour Clauses
content:
Mandatory clauses in supplier code of conduct:
MINIMUM WAGES: Suppliers must pay at least local legal minimum wage or industry standard (whichever is higher) plus statutory benefits.
WORKING HOURS: Maximum 48 hours per week normal working hours, max 60 hours including overtime. Overtime voluntary and fairly compensated (at least 1.5x regular rate).
FREE TIME: Minimum one rest day per 7 days, plus statutory public holidays.
CHILD LABOUR: No workers under 15 (or local school-leaving age). Under 18s not permitted in hazardous work.
FORCED LABOUR: Zero tolerance. No wage deductions except legal requirements. All work voluntary.
FREEDOM OF ASSOCIATION: Workers may join or form unions; suppliers must not interfere or discriminate.

Seasonal stock provisioning rules:
- Summer season (May-August): order stock to cover forecast + 20% safety stock
- Winter season (November-December): order to cover forecast + 30% safety stock due to higher volatility
- Spring/Autumn: 15% safety stock
Slow-moving inventory:
- Aged 90-180 days: offer at 15% discount to sales team
- Aged 180+ days: 30% markdown; mark down further per NRV policy
- Fashion items >3 seasons old: write off
Inventory turns by category:
- Fashion: minimum 4x annual
- Home: minimum 2x annual
- Electronics: minimum 6x annual

Customer Recall Notice:
'This product batch [BATCH] may [DEFECT]. If you own this product, please [ACTION]. Return it to any store for full refund. For questions: [PHONE/EMAIL]. Thank you for your patience.'

Store Instructions (internal):
'Remove batch [BATCH] from sale immediately. Do not process returns on this batch. Direct customers to Customer Service. Destroy stock per instructions [LINK].'

Press Statement (pre-approved language):
'We have voluntarily recalled batch [BATCH] due to [ISSUE]. No injuries reported. This affects approximately [UNITS] units sold [DATES]. Affected customers should contact Customer Service.'

Regulatory Notification (formal):
'Harbour & Vale Retail Group notifies [REGULATOR] of the recall of [PRODUCT] batch [BATCH]. Reason: [REASON]. Notification date: [DATE]. Distribution area: [AREA]. Contact: [NAME, PHONE].'

RECALL: Proactive removal from market because product poses safety or serious performance risk.
Triggers: Death/serious injury risk, regulatory violation (e.g. banned material), widespread defect affecting >1% of batch.
Action: Notify regulator within 24-72 hours (varies by country/product). Issue customer recall notice. Seek publicity (press release, media).

WITHDRAWAL: Reactive removal after limited complaints or merchant request. No imminent safety risk.
Triggers: Cosmetic defect, minor performance gap, customer returns, merchant delisting request.
Action: Do NOT notify public. Notify regulator if required by law. Offer merchant replacement/credit. No media.

UK timeline:
Recall: Notify within 24 hours of decision. Escalate to local authorities.
Withdrawal: Notify within 2 weeks or as scheduled.
EU/US: Tighter timelines (6-12 hours for safety issues).

TCFD (Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures):
- Governance: Board oversight of climate risk
- Strategy: Climate scenarios, financial impact
- Risk Management: Process for identifying, assessing climate risks
- Metrics: GHG emissions (Scope 1, 2, 3), energy, financial metrics
- Deadline: Recommended for all companies; mandatory for listed entities from 2025

GRI (Global Reporting Initiative):
- GRI 305 (Emissions): Scope 1, 2, 3 emissions, intensity
- GRI 403 (Occupational Health & Safety): Injuries, fatalities, hazard assessment
- GRI 407 (Freedom of Association): Assessed facilities, assessed countries
- Data evidence: Supplier questionnaires, audit reports, conversion factors

CSRD (Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive):
- Double materiality: What impacts the business + what the business impacts
- Scope 1, 2, 3 emissions; water; waste; biodiversity; social risks
- Supply chain due diligence mandatory
- Third-party assurance required (ISAE 3410/3000)

ISSB (International Sustainability Standards Board):
- IFRS S1 (General sustainability): Governance, strategy, risk, metrics
- IFRS S2 (Climate): Same as TCFD

policy_name: Responsible Exit Policy and Worker Protection
content:
When exiting a supplier (suspension, termination, or market exit):

1. ADVANCE NOTICE (minimum 90 days): Communicate timeline to supplier and affected workers through union/worker representatives.

2. FINANCIAL OBLIGATIONS:
   - Pay all wages owed plus statutory benefits through exit date
   - Provide redundancy compensation per local law (minimum 2 weeks per year of service)
   - Settle any pension/provident fund obligations
   - Ensure health insurance continuation during notice period

3. WORKER SUPPORT:
   - Facilitate retraining and job placement (fund if supplier cannot)
   - Provide documentation for future employment (work history, certifications)
   - Allow union access for worker communication
   - Grievance mechanism for wage/benefit disputes

4. PRODUCTION CONTINUITY:
   - Transition orders to alternative suppliers gradually
   - Do NOT suspend all POs immediately; phase over 90+ days to allow worker absorption
   - Support worker access to final orders for wages

5. MONITORING:
   - Verify wages paid during notice period
   - Confirm no worker retaliation or blacklisting
   - Follow up post-exit (6 months) on worker outcome

Claims review checklist to ensure marketing claims pass ASA, CMA and EU greenwashing rules:

SUBSTANTIATION:
- Do we hold independent third-party evidence (ISO 14040 LCA, Product Environmental Footprint, certification)?
- Is data current (not >3 years old)? Is sample representative (≥5% of production or clear justification)?
- Have we disclosed methodology and benchmark comparators (if any)?

WORDING:
- Avoid absolute terms ('100% sustainable', 'eco-friendly' without qualification)
- Avoid time-based claims without baseline ('20% reduction since 2020' - baseline stated?)
- Avoid implied certifications (if claiming ISO cert, state it explicitly)
- Disclose trade-offs ('lower carbon BUT higher water use')
- Clear scope: product level? Company level? Supply chain?

REGULATORY RISK:
- Check recent ASA/CMA enforcement (monthly update)
- Are similar claims in recent enforcement cases?
- Legal review sign-off required before ANY publication

HIGH-RISK CLAIMS:
- 'Sustainable', 'eco-friendly', 'green' without qualifier
- Comparative claims vs competitors
- Percentage reductions without baseline
- Any claim using unverified third-party sources
